Subject: POC plan & success criteria — MedBase public health pilot

Hi Samantha / Carlos,

Thanks again for the productive discovery call earlier — great alignment on use cases (clinical note summarization for case management + PHI-redaction for downstream analytics). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- POC goal: validate Redwood inference performance and safety for MedBase anonymized notes pipeline; prove latency, accuracy, and PHI-redaction before procurement signs SOW.
- Proposed scope: 4-week trial using a 1000-note sample set you provide (anonymized) + two integration tests (batch export, streaming API).
- Success criteria (draft):
  - >= 95% PHI redaction recall on your sample set
  - Median latency <= 150ms per token for 512-token runs
  - Qualitative score >= 8/10 from your clinical reviewers on summary utility
- Ownership: Redwood SE (Dev) will run infra + baseline evals; Marissa will coordinate timelines and contracting; MedBase will provide dataset, evaluation rubric, and exec stakeholders for final readout.

Action items from our side: Dev to send a one-page POC plan + milestone dates (ETA: EOD Thu). From your side: confirm success criteria and availability for a final readout the week of Jul 20.

I copied Rishi for visibility on contract/flex options. Let me know if you want any changes and we’ll lock the dates.

Thanks,

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

Hi Samantha / Carlos —

Attached is a draft POC plan that lays out the technical milestones, evaluation plan, and timelines we discussed. High-level items:

1) Week 0 (prep): data handoff, access keys, test workspace, and baseline model selection.
2) Week 1: initial ingest + PHI-redaction run, baseline metrics (recall/precision).
3) Week 2: summary generation + human review (your clinical reviewers), iterative prompt tuning.
4) Week 3: integration test (batch export and API streaming), latency load test.
5) Week 4: final readout prep + executive summary.

Success criteria are included in the attached PDF (spreadsheet version requested if you want to drop in your rubric). We’ve flagged integration test scenarios for PHI-handling and end-to-end latency under realistic batching.

Attachments: [Attachment: MedBase_POC_plan.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

Can you confirm: (a) dataset delivery date, (b) who on your side will do the clinical scoring, and (c) whether you need Redwood to run the human review sessions or MedBase will do them internally?

If all good, propose we kickoff the week of Jun 15 to keep the July 20 readout week intact.

Thanks,
Dev
——

Thanks, Marissa and Dev — the plan looks good. A few notes from our side after internal review:

- Dataset: We can deliver the 1,000-note anonymized sample on Tue Jun 16.
- Clinical scoring: Dr. Priya Natarajan and two clinical reviewers will score summaries (we will share rubric in XLSX).
- Success criteria addendum: Please include a PHI redaction false-positive check (to ensure clinical meaning preserved) and an end-to-end 99th percentile latency target in addition to median.
- Procurement: procurement@medbase.com is the contact for SOW & pricing — likely needs a 2–3 week review cycle.

Attaching our scoring template for reference. We agree to a kickoff Jun 17 and target readout week of Jul 20.

- Redwood can run the human review sessions if you prefer; otherwise we’ll provide the tooling and the reviewers can score in-place. Which do you prefer?
